from.place: Finite-field proof, finite modules: degree-two cyclic inflation for constant prime coefficients

title: Finite-field degree-two vanishing with constant prime coefficients
statement: Let K be a finite field, Ks a separable closure of K [def-pd-separable-closure], and ell a prime nonzero in K. Put G = Gal(Ks/K) with its Krull topology. The degree-two continuous cohomology H²(G, Z/ell), for the trivial discrete action and with cohomology as in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], vanishes. In the Lean presentation this is Ext² from the trivial integer module in the category of discrete abelian G-modules; the coefficient group is ULift of ZMod ell in universe u+1.

source.place: Finite modules and Consequences: specialize the cyclic-inflation argument to degree two and trivial prime coefficients prime to the characteristic

proof.text: Apply finiteField_absoluteGaloisGroup from det-base-field-cd-galois-group. Its continuous group isomorphism identifies Frobenius tau with the canonical image of 1 in the profinite completion of the integers. Pull density of the canonical map back across the isomorphism to obtain density of the integral powers of tau. The universal property of the profinite completion extends each integer residue homomorphism to a continuous map G→Z/n sending tau to 1.

source.place: Finite modules paragraph: refining a cyclic quotient by the coefficient exponent; explicit finite summation implementation of this argument

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-profinite-integer-smooth-primitives to smooth functions G→ULift(ZMod ell). Every value is killed by ell, so translation by tau minus identity is surjective on the coinduced module I(X). Passing to the explicit quotient C(X)=I(X)/X shows it is surjective on C(X) as well. This is the finite cyclic refinement argument at the level of explicit primitives; it avoids the comparison of cochain and Ext cohomology.

source.place: Finite modules paragraph: refining a cyclic quotient by the coefficient exponent; explicit finite summation implementation of this argument

proof.text: For a discrete module Y on which tau-1 is surjective, prove H^1(G,Y)=0 using the proved source lemmas subsingleton_ext_one_iff, shortExact₁, subsingleton_H_coind₁ and forall_exists_comp_eq_iff. An invariant class in I(Y)/Y lifts to f. The difference tau*f-f is the image of some x in Y. Choose y with tau*y-y=x and subtract the image of y from f. The resulting lift is fixed by tau, hence by all G: its stabilizer is open, therefore closed, and contains every integral power of tau. Its quotient class is unchanged. Thus every invariant class lifts to an invariant element and the Ext exact sequence gives H^1=0.

proof.text: Apply the previous step to C(X), using surjectivity from step 2. The short exact sequence 0→X→I(X)→C(X)→0 and the proved acyclicity of I(X) identify H^2(G,X) as a quotient of H^1(G,C(X)), by subsingleton_ext_succ_of_shortExact. This proves the required subsingleton statement without changing any hypotheses or coefficient universes.
